lessons.title: Notre environnement naturel
lessons.oneGoal: Students will identify different natural environments around them and recognize that they are part of these environments

opening.activity: Nature sounds listening game - students close eyes and identify different environmental sounds
opening.visualSupports: large poster showing different natural environments (forest, water, garden, field)

main.activity: Environment exploration walk around school grounds or nature picture sorting and discussion
main.visualSupports: environment identification chart, 'I am part of nature' poster

decisionPoints.question: Can students safely explore outdoors?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Take nature walk to identify local environments
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use window observations and picture sorting activities

decisionPoints.question: Do students understand they are part of the environment?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Discuss how their actions affect nature
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on simple observation and identification first

closing.activity: Circle share - students share one natural environment they found and how they are part of it

troubleshooting.then: Compare natural spaces (trees, grass) with human-made spaces (buildings, roads)

lessons.realWorldConnection: Recognizing the parks, forests, beaches, or gardens in their neighborhood as natural environments

lessons.title: Les animaux dans leur maison naturelle
lessons.oneGoal: Students will observe and identify where different animals live in natural environments

opening.activity: Animal home guessing game - show animal pictures and guess where they live
opening.visualSupports: animal homes matching poster (bird-tree, fish-water, rabbit-burrow)

main.activity: Create simple animal habitat dioramas using natural and craft materials
main.visualSupports: habitat examples poster, step-by-step diorama instructions

decisionPoints.question: Can students match animals to correct habitats?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Explore why specific animals need specific homes
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on obvious examples like fish needing water

closing.activity: Habitat gallery walk - students present their dioramas and explain animal homes

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: understanding why animals need specific habitats
troubleshooting.then: Use familiar examples like pets needing safe, comfortable homes

lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding where birds build nests, where squirrels live, and where fish swim

lessons.title: Les plantes ont leur place aussi
lessons.oneGoal: Students will identify where different plants grow naturally and why location matters for plants

opening.activity: Plant location detective game - examine plants in different school locations
opening.visualSupports: plant location preference chart (sun plants, shade plants, water plants)

main.activity: Plant a classroom experiment with same seeds in different conditions (light, dark, wet, dry)
main.visualSupports: plant needs diagram, experiment tracking chart

decisionPoints.question: Do students understand plants have location preferences?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Explore what happens when plants are in wrong locations
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on simple observations of where plants look healthy

closing.activity: Plant placement predictions - students predict which planted seeds will grow best

troubleshooting.then: Compare to humans needing appropriate places to live and be healthy

lessons.realWorldConnection: Noticing why certain plants grow in gardens, forests, or near water

lessons.title: Tout est connecté dans la nature
lessons.oneGoal: Students will discover simple connections between animals, plants, and their environment

opening.activity: Connection web game - hold yarn to show how students are connected to each other
opening.visualSupports: nature connection web poster showing plant-animal relationships

main.activity: Create nature connection chains using pictures and arrows to show relationships
main.visualSupports: simple food chain examples, connection word bank

decisionPoints.question: Can students identify simple connections (bird eats seeds)?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Explore what happens when connections are broken
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on very obvious connections like animals needing plants for food

closing.activity: Connection sharing circle - students share one nature connection they discovered

troubleshooting.then: Use very concrete examples like 'bird needs tree for nest, tree needs bird to spread seeds'

lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding how birds need trees for nests and trees need birds to spread seeds

lessons.title: L'eau: source de vie partout
lessons.oneGoal: Students will recognize that all living things need clean water and identify water sources in nature

opening.activity: Water needs demonstration - show how plants, animals, and humans all need water
opening.visualSupports: water cycle poster, clean vs polluted water pictures

main.activity: Create a classroom water filter using natural materials and test with muddy water
main.visualSupports: water filtration diagram, natural water sources map

decisionPoints.question: Do students understand water quality matters for all life?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Explore what makes water clean or dirty
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on simple observation that all living things drink water

closing.activity: Water protection pledges - students share one way they will help keep water clean

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: understanding why water needs to be clean
troubleshooting.then: Compare to drinking water at home and why we wouldn't drink dirty water

lessons.realWorldConnection: Recognizing rivers, lakes, rain, and drinking water as essential for all life

lessons.title: L'air pur pour tous les vivants
lessons.oneGoal: Students will understand that all living things need clean air and identify what helps keep air clean

opening.activity: Breathing awareness exercise - students notice how they breathe and what clean air feels like
opening.visualSupports: air quality poster, trees cleaning air diagram

main.activity: Plant air filters experiment - compare air quality near plants vs away from plants using simple tests
main.visualSupports: how trees clean air poster, air pollution examples

decisionPoints.question: Can students understand that trees help clean air?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Explore other things that help or hurt air quality
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on simple observation that plants and trees are good for air

closing.activity: Fresh air appreciation walk - students take deep breaths and appreciate clean air

troubleshooting.then: Use familiar examples like how nice it smells in forests vs near cars

lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding why trees are important and why we avoid polluting the air

lessons.title: Prendre soin de notre environnement
lessons.oneGoal: Students will identify simple ways they can help take care of their natural environment

opening.activity: Environmental care photo analysis - look at before/after pictures of environmental care actions
opening.visualSupports: environmental care actions poster, 'Earth helpers' chart

main.activity: Environmental care action planning - choose and practice simple care actions for school environment
main.visualSupports: step-by-step care action guides, environmental care pledge chart

decisionPoints.question: Are students ready to take responsibility for environmental care?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Plan regular care actions for the classroom/school
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on simple, one-time care actions to build confidence

closing.activity: Environmental care pledge ceremony - students make commitments to care for their environment

troubleshooting.then: Focus on small, positive actions that make students feel empowered

lessons.realWorldConnection: Learning how picking up litter, not disturbing animals, and caring for plants helps everyone

lessons.title: Réduire nos déchets
lessons.oneGoal: Students will understand that making less waste helps protect the environment and identify ways to reduce waste

opening.activity: Classroom waste audit - examine what gets thrown away in one day
opening.visualSupports: waste reduction poster, 'less waste = happier Earth' chart

main.activity: Waste reduction challenge - students brainstorm and practice ways to make less waste
main.visualSupports: waste reduction strategies poster, before/after waste examples

decisionPoints.question: Can students identify specific waste reduction actions?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Practice implementing waste reduction in classroom activities
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on simple examples like using both sides of paper

closing.activity: Waste reduction commitment ceremony - students choose one waste reduction action to practice

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: understanding the connection between waste and environmental harm
troubleshooting.then: Use simple examples like litter hurting animals or filling up nature spaces

lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding how using both sides of paper and bringing reusable water bottles helps nature

lessons.title: Réutiliser les objets créativement
lessons.oneGoal: Students will discover how to give objects new purposes instead of throwing them away

opening.activity: Magic transformation game - show how common items can become something new
opening.visualSupports: reuse transformation examples poster, 'new life for old things' chart

main.activity: Create useful items from materials that would otherwise be discarded
main.visualSupports: step-by-step reuse project guides, reuse safety rules poster

decisionPoints.question: Are students able to see new possibilities for discarded items?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Encourage creative, original reuse ideas
decisionPoints.ifNo: Provide specific examples and guided reuse projects

closing.activity: Reuse creation showcase - students share their new creations and explain the transformation

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: seeing creative possibilities in discarded items
troubleshooting.then: Start with very obvious transformations like containers becoming organizers

lessons.realWorldConnection: Learning how empty containers can become plant pots and old clothes can become cleaning rags

lessons.title: Le recyclage: donner une nouvelle vie
lessons.oneGoal: Students will understand how recycling transforms old materials into new products

opening.activity: Recycling transformation demonstration - show paper being made from recycled materials
opening.visualSupports: recycling process poster, 'from old to new' transformation chart

main.activity: Make recycled paper or participate in simple recycling transformation activity
main.visualSupports: recycling step-by-step guides, materials transformation examples

decisionPoints.question: Do students understand that recycling changes materials into new products?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Explore different types of recycling transformations
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on one clear example like paper becoming new paper

closing.activity: Recycling transformation celebration - students share their recycled creations

troubleshooting.then: Use very concrete before/after examples with familiar materials

lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding how paper becomes new paper and bottles become new products

lessons.title: Trier pour mieux recycler
lessons.oneGoal: Students will learn to sort different materials for recycling and understand why sorting helps

opening.activity: Recycling sorting race - quickly sort mixed recyclables into correct categories
opening.visualSupports: recycling sorting guide poster, material identification chart

main.activity: Create classroom recycling station with proper sorting system
main.visualSupports: recycling symbols guide, sorting decision tree poster

decisionPoints.question: Can students accurately sort materials by type?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Introduce more challenging materials and recycling symbols
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on basic categories (paper, plastic, metal) with clear examples

closing.activity: Sorting expertise test - students demonstrate their sorting skills

troubleshooting.then: Create simple sorting songs or rhymes to help remember categories

lessons.realWorldConnection: Learning why families have different bins for paper, plastic, and other recyclables

lessons.title: Les 3 R: Réduire, Réutiliser, Recycler
lessons.oneGoal: Students will understand and apply the 3 Rs as a strategy for helping the environment

opening.activity: 3 Rs song and movement activity - learn actions for reduce, reuse, recycle
opening.visualSupports: 3 Rs hierarchy poster showing order of preference, action reminder chart

main.activity: 3 Rs decision-making scenarios - practice choosing the best R for different situations
main.visualSupports: 3 Rs decision flowchart, scenario examples poster

decisionPoints.question: Do students understand the order of the 3 Rs (reduce first, then reuse, then recycle)?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Practice applying 3 Rs to complex scenarios
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on simple examples where the best choice is obvious

closing.activity: 3 Rs pledge ceremony - students commit to using the 3 Rs strategy in their daily lives

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: remembering the order of the 3 Rs
troubleshooting.then: Use the hierarchy as a ladder: reduce at top, recycle at bottom

lessons.realWorldConnection: Having a simple strategy to follow when deciding what to do with items at home and school

lessons.title: Notre projet de compostage
lessons.oneGoal: Students will create a simple compost system and understand how food scraps become soil

opening.activity: Decomposition demonstration - show different stages of food waste breakdown
opening.visualSupports: composting process poster, 'from scraps to soil' transformation chart

main.activity: Build classroom compost bin and add first materials
main.visualSupports: composting recipe poster, compost care instructions chart

decisionPoints.question: Can students understand the composting process?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Assign students different composting care responsibilities
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on simple observation of materials changing over time

closing.activity: Compost care commitment ceremony - students sign up for compost monitoring duties

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: understanding how food waste becomes soil
troubleshooting.then: Compare to leaves falling and becoming part of forest floor naturally

lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding how kitchen scraps can help garden plants grow better

lessons.title: Économiser l'énergie ensemble
lessons.oneGoal: Students will identify simple ways to save energy at home and school to help the environment

opening.activity: Energy use detective walk - identify how energy is used in the classroom and school
opening.visualSupports: energy sources poster, energy conservation actions chart

main.activity: Create energy-saving action plan for classroom and practice energy conservation
main.visualSupports: energy saving tips poster, 'energy helpers' chart

decisionPoints.question: Can students identify energy waste in their environment?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Create systematic energy conservation plan with specific responsibilities
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on obvious examples like turning off lights when leaving room

closing.activity: Energy conservation pledge - students commit to specific energy-saving actions

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: understanding why saving energy helps environment
troubleshooting.then: Use simple examples like 'less energy use means cleaner air for animals'

lessons.realWorldConnection: Learning why turning off lights and using less hot water helps protect nature

lessons.title: Créer un jardin pour les pollinisateurs
lessons.oneGoal: Students will plant flowers to help bees and butterflies and understand how this helps the ecosystem

opening.activity: Pollinator observation - watch videos or observe real pollinators visiting flowers
opening.visualSupports: pollinator identification poster, flower-pollinator matching chart

main.activity: Plant pollinator-friendly flowers in containers or school garden
main.visualSupports: pollinator garden planning poster, flower care instructions

decisionPoints.question: Do students understand how flowers help pollinators and pollinators help plants?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Explore what happens when pollinators have no flowers to visit
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on simple observation that bees and butterflies love flowers

closing.activity: Pollinator garden blessing ceremony - students make wishes for their flowers to help pollinators

troubleshooting.then: Use simple analogy like pollinators visiting flowers like people visiting restaurants

lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding how helping bees and butterflies helps flowers and food grow

lessons.title: Les transports respectueux de l'environnement
lessons.oneGoal: Students will identify transportation choices that help keep air and environment clean

opening.activity: Transportation survey - chart how students get to school and discuss environmental impact
opening.visualSupports: clean transportation options poster, air quality comparison chart

main.activity: Green transportation challenge - plan and practice environmentally-friendly transportation
main.visualSupports: green transportation benefits poster, local walking/biking route map

decisionPoints.question: Can students connect transportation choices to environmental impact?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Calculate environmental benefits of green transportation choices
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on simple observation that walking/biking creates no pollution

closing.activity: Green transportation pledge - students commit to using clean transportation when possible

troubleshooting.then: Use visible examples like seeing exhaust from cars vs no exhaust from bicycles

lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding why walking to school or taking the bus can help keep air clean

lessons.title: Protéger les animaux sauvages
lessons.oneGoal: Students will learn respectful ways to observe and protect wild animals in their natural habitats

opening.activity: Wildlife observation practice - learn proper techniques for watching animals without disturbing them
opening.visualSupports: wildlife watching rules poster, respectful distance guidelines chart

main.activity: Create wildlife protection action plan for school grounds and local environment
main.visualSupports: wildlife protection strategies poster, habitat protection examples

decisionPoints.question: Do students understand how human actions affect wildlife?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Plan specific habitat protection actions for school environment
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on simple rules like not chasing or bothering animals

closing.activity: Wildlife protection pledge ceremony - students commit to protecting local wildlife

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: understanding why animals need protection from humans
troubleshooting.then: Compare to how students need safe, quiet spaces to feel comfortable

lessons.realWorldConnection: Learning how to watch birds and animals safely without disturbing their homes

lessons.title: Partager notre planète équitablement
lessons.oneGoal: Students will understand that all living things need space and resources and practice sharing environmental spaces

opening.activity: Playground sharing reflection - discuss how students share playground space fairly
opening.visualSupports: fair sharing principles poster, environmental sharing examples chart

main.activity: Design fair use plan for school natural spaces that considers all living things
main.visualSupports: environmental justice examples poster, sharing solutions chart

decisionPoints.question: Can students apply fairness concepts to environmental sharing?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Explore complex sharing scenarios with multiple needs
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on simple examples like leaving some areas for wildlife

closing.activity: Environmental sharing pledge - students commit to fair environmental sharing practices

troubleshooting.then: Use familiar sharing examples from home and school to build understanding

lessons.realWorldConnection: Understanding why everyone needs access to clean parks, water, and natural spaces

lessons.title: Devenir des ambassadeurs de l'environnement
lessons.oneGoal: Students will teach others about caring for the environment and share their environmental knowledge

opening.activity: Ambassador preparation - students choose their best environmental learning to share
opening.visualSupports: teaching strategies poster, environmental knowledge showcase examples

main.activity: Create environmental education presentations for younger students or family members
main.visualSupports: presentation structure guide, environmental teaching tips poster

decisionPoints.question: Are students confident in their environmental knowledge?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Prepare presentations for authentic teaching opportunities
decisionPoints.ifNo: Practice with classmates first to build confidence

closing.activity: Ambassador commissioning ceremony - students receive environmental educator certificates

troubleshooting.then: Start with sharing one simple environmental tip with a friend or family member

lessons.realWorldConnection: Building confidence to teach family members about environmental care actions

lessons.title: Célébration de notre environnement partagé
lessons.oneGoal: Students will celebrate their environmental learning by showcasing actions they've taken and commitments for the future

opening.activity: Environmental journey reflection - students review all their environmental learning and actions
opening.visualSupports: environmental learning journey timeline, student achievement showcase

main.activity: Environmental fair - students showcase projects, demonstrate skills, and share commitments
main.visualSupports: student work displays, environmental action evidence board

decisionPoints.question: Are students able to articulate their environmental learning growth?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Focus celebration on student-led demonstrations and teaching
decisionPoints.ifNo: Provide structured ways for students to share their learning

closing.activity: Environmental stewardship pledge renewal - students make commitments for continued environmental care

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: seeing themselves as capable environmental stewards
troubleshooting.then: Highlight specific examples of their successful environmental actions throughout the unit

lessons.realWorldConnection: Sharing our environmental care actions with families and community to inspire continued environmental protection
